<issue identifier="MM-417">
<title>Notify 3/9: relay APNs pipeline — ES256 JWT, HTTP/2 push, size validation, 410 feedback</title>
<description>
Phase 3 of the <issue id="b95fcd23-95fa-43f6-86a6-81defb9dda77" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-311/e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-custos-apns">MM-311</issue> notification relay. Implementation details: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md`.

## Scope

Complete the `push` RPC in `crates/notify-relay`:

* **APNs client:** reqwest (workspace 0.13, rustls — ALPN-negotiates h2 against real APNs, h1 against wiremock). Token auth is a **hand-rolled ES256 JWT** over the existing `p256` dep (~30 lines: `{alg, kid}` header + `{iss: team_id, iat}` claims, base64url, ECDSA-sign) — avoids `jsonwebtoken`'s `ring` dependency. Cached, refreshed at 50 min per Apple's 20–60 min rule.
* **Request assembly:** envelope `{"aps": {"alert": {"title": "Custos", "body": "Encrypted notification"}, "mutable-content": 1}, "ezpds": {"v": 1, "kid", "enc", "ct"}}`; headers `apns-topic` (from the handle row — per-handle topics), `apns-push-type`, `apns-priority`, `apns-expiration` (now + ttlSecs). Endpoint overridable via `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL` (the wiremock seam, same trick as `EZPDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL`).
* **Size validation:** enforce the 4096-byte cap on the fully serialized APNs body server-side (defense in depth against a misbehaving sender) → `tooLarge`.
* **Outcome mapping:** APNs 200 → `delivered`, **410 →** `unregistered` (the pruning back-channel — returned synchronously in the push RPC response), 429/5xx → `apnsError`; per-handle rate bucket (60/h default) → `throttled`.

## Acceptance

* Wiremock-APNs tests: happy path (assert topic/priority/expiration headers + envelope shape), 410 maps to `unregistered`, oversize rejected with a boundary test at exactly 4096 bytes, JWT cached across pushes and refreshed after expiry.
* Loopback e2e: enroll → registerHandle → push → mock APNs receives the request.
</description>
<team name="Mal's Machinations"/>
<label>Feature</label>
<project name="ezpds">An easy-to-host PDS on the ATProtocol, MacOS. Grandma-approved.</project>

<title>E2E-encrypted notification relay for self-hosted Custos (APNs)</title>
<description>
Implement the notification relay designed in [docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](<https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/blob/main/docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md>) (design PR <pull-request id="34230e45-6259-4c9a-b58d-6b135adf84e3" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/design-exploration-e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-327f880332d1">malpercio-dev/ezpds#207</pull-request>, **merged** — the doc on `main` is the source of truth and incorporates the review hardening: claim-code enrollment authorization for the official relay, versioned sender keys with re-pin/revocation semantics, explicit v1 replay acceptance, unverified-notice rendering for unauthenticated payloads, per-handle APNs topics, serialized-request padding budget, and the post-reboot keychain window).

## Problem

Self-hosted Custos instances need to deliver push notifications to the official iOS apps (Obsign, admin-companion). APNs auth keys are bundle-ID-bound, so self-hosters cannot push directly — a relay is structurally required. The design makes that relay a **blind courier**: trusted for availability only.

## Architecture (see design doc for full detail)

* **Confidentiality:** payloads HPKE-sealed (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-GCM) to a per-device notification key; decrypted on-device by a Notification Service Extension (`mutable-content: 1`). Neither the relay nor Apple sees plaintext.
* **Integrity:** HPKE Auth mode with pinned, versioned per-instance sender keys — the relay cannot forge authenticated content (it can generate detectable junk pushes and replay; v1 accepts duplicates as benign).
* **Metadata minimization:** opaque push handles bound to the instance's iroh node id (no DIDs/handles/raw tokens at the relay), fixed-size padding budgeted against the serialized APNs request, optional content-free ping mode.
* **Transport:** Custos ↔ relay over iroh, new `ezpds/notify/0` ALPN, reusing the persisted node identity (`iroh_identity`) and `iroh_tunnel.rs` patterns; back-channel carries APNs `410 Unregistered` pruning feedback.
* **Sovereignty:** relay is an open-source workspace crate (`crates/notify-relay/`); any instance points at any relay via `[notifications] relay = "<node id>"`. Official relay requires a claim-code enrollment grant; open enrollment is a config option for self-run relays. Caveat: official bundle IDs require the official relay's APNs key.

## Suggested phasing

1. **Relay crate + Custos sender** — `crates/notify-relay/` (claim-code enrollment grants, handle store with per-handle APNs topic, APNs HTTP/2 client, per-node rate limits, serialized-request size validation with 4 KB boundary test) + `[notifications]` config, device notification-key registration route, versioned sender-key set, sealed-send on first trigger (agent claim pending). Loopback iroh e2e tests with mock APNs.
2. **Wallet NSE** — per-device keypair + shared keychain access group, registration in onboarding, decrypt-and-render extension, unverified-notice fallback + in-app diagnostics.
3. **Admin-companion adoption + operator docs** — ops alert triggers, self-relay runbook, metadata-minimizing ping mode.

## Open questions (from the design doc)

* Enrollment grant distribution for the official relay (ceremony mirrors admin-device pairing)
* Replay hardening beyond v1's accept-duplicates posture (per-device counter + durable replay window)
* Delivery receipts over the iroh back-channel (out of scope v1)
* Android/FCM later (envelope is provider-agnostic)

Not yet scheduled into a wave; split into per-phase issues when picked up.
</description>
</parent-issue>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- ed3d-basic-agents:haiku-general-purpose: An unprompted generic subagent. Uses Haiku. Intended for tasks that require less thinking and analysis. Good for summarization, research, and tool calls. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-basic-agents:opus-general-purpose: An unprompted generic subagent. Uses Opus. Intended for tasks that require deep reasoning, complex analysis, or nuanced judgment. (Tools: All tools except Agent)
- ed3d-basic-agents:sonnet-general-purpose: An unprompted generic subagent. Uses Sonnet. Intended for tasks that require attention to detail, thinking, and analysis. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-extending-claude:project-claude-librarian: Use when completing development phases and project context files may need updating - analyzes what changed since phase start, identifies affected CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md files, and coordinates updates to maintain accurate project documentation (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:code-reviewer: Reviews completed project steps against plans and enforces coding standards. Use when a numbered step from a plan is complete, a major feature is implemented, or before creating a PR. Validates plan alignment, code quality, test coverage, and architecture. Blocks merges for Minor, Important, or Critical issues. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:task-bug-fixer: Fixes issues identified by code-reviewer and triggers re-review. Use when code-reviewer returns any issues that need to be addressed before merge approval. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:task-implementor-fast: Implements individual tasks from plans with TDD, skill application, verification, and git commits. Use when executing a specific task that requires writing, modifying, or testing code as part of a larger plan. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:test-analyst: Use after final code review passes to validate test coverage against acceptance criteria and generate human test plans - reads test-requirements.md, verifies automated tests exist, produces manual verification documentation (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-playwright:playwright-explorer: Use when exploring websites, proving hypotheses about web application behavior, automating browser interactions, or generating E2E tests - investigates page structure through accessibility snapshots, tests assumptions systematically, and coordinates Playwright MCP tools with tenacity to complete complex multi-step investigations (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:codebase-investigator: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need to understand current codebase state, find existing patterns, or verify assumptions about what exists. Examples: <example>Context: Starting brainstorming phase and need to understand current authentication implementation. user: "I want to add OAuth support to our app" assistant: "Let me use the codebase-investigator agent to understand how authentication currently works before we design the OAuth integration" <commentary>Before designing new features, investigate existing patterns to ensure the design builds on what's already there.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Writing implementation plan and need to verify file locations and current structure. user: "Create a plan for adding user profiles" assistant: "I'll use the codebase-investigator agent to verify the current user model structure and find where user-related code lives" <commentary>Investigation prevents hallucinating file paths or assuming structure that doesn't exist.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:combined-researcher: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need current information BOTH the local system AND from the internet, API documentation, library usage patterns, or external knowledge. Examples: <example>Context: Designing integration with external service and need to understand current API. user: "I want to integrate with the Stripe API for payments" assistant: "Let me use the combined-researcher agent to find if and how we currently use Stripe, and then the current Stripe API documentation and best practices for integration" <commentary>Before designing integrations, research current API state and current local codebase state to ensure plan matches reality.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Evaluating technology choices for implementation plan. user: "Should we use library X or Y for this feature?" assistant: "I'll use the combined-researcher agent to research what we've currently selected already, then if we haven't selected something we'll look at both libraries' current status, features, and community recommendations" <commentary>Research helps make informed technology decisions based on current information.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:internet-researcher: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need current information from the internet, API documentation, library usage patterns, or external knowledge. Examples: <example>Context: Designing integration with external service and need to understand current API. user: "I want to integrate with the Stripe API for payments" assistant: "Let me use the internet-researcher agent to find the current Stripe API documentation and best practices for integration" <commentary>Before designing integrations, research current API state to ensure plan matches reality.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Evaluating technology choices for implementation plan. user: "Should we use library X or Y for this feature?" assistant: "I'll use the internet-researcher agent to research both libraries' current status, features, and community recommendations" <commentary>Research helps make informed technology decisions based on current information.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:remote-code-researcher: Use when understanding how external libraries or open-source projects implement features by examining actual source code - finds repos via web search, clones to a stable cache directory, investigates with codebase analysis. Triggers: "how does library X implement Y", "show me how Z handles this", "I want to see the actual code for", evaluating library internals before adoption. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-session-reflection:conversation-reviewer: Use when reviewing a Claude Code session transcript for quality — analyzes human prompting effectiveness, agent performance patterns, and environment/tooling gaps, then writes structured findings to a specified output file. Requires a reduced transcript path and output path. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- episodic-memory:search-conversations: Gives you memory across sessions. You don't automatically remember past conversations - THIS AGENT RESTORES IT. Search your history before starting any task to recover decisions, solutions, and lessons learned. (Tools: Read, mcp__plugin_episodic-memory_episodic-memory__search, mcp__plugin_episodic-memory_episodic-memory__show)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/linear-workflow

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

{"id":"MM-417","title":"Notify 3/9: relay APNs pipeline — ES256 JWT, HTTP/2 push, size validation, 410 feedback","description":"Phase 3 of the <issue id="b95fcd23-95fa-43f6-86a6-81defb9dda77" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-311/e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-custos-apns">MM-311</issue> notification relay. Implementation details: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md`.

## Scope

Complete the `push` RPC in `crates/notify-relay`:

* **APNs client:** reqwest (workspace 0.13, rustls — ALPN-negotiates h2 against real APNs, h1 against wiremock). Token auth is a **hand-rolled ES256 JWT** over the existing `p256` dep (~30 lines: `{alg, kid}` header + `{iss: team_id, iat}` claims, base64url, ECDSA-sign) — avoids `jsonwebtoken`'s `ring` dependency. Cached, refreshed at 50 min per Apple's 20–60 min rule.
* **Request assembly:** envelope `{"aps": {"alert": {"title": "Custos", "body": "Encrypted notification"}, "mutable-content": 1}, "ezpds": {"v": 1, "kid", "enc", "ct"}}`; headers `apns-topic` (from the handle row — per-handle topics), `apns-push-type`, `apns-priority`, `apns-expiration` (now + ttlSecs). Endpoint overridable via `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL` (the wiremock seam, same trick as `EZPDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL`).
* **Size validation:** enforce the 4096-byte cap on the fully serialized APNs body server-side (defense in depth against a misbehaving sender) → `tooLarge`.
* **Outcome mapping:** APNs 200 → `delivered`, **410 →** `unregistered` (the pruning back-channel — returned synchronously in the push RPC response), 429/5xx → `apnsError`; per-handle rate bucket (60/h default) → `throttled`.

## Acceptance

* Wiremock-APNs tests: happy path (assert topic/priority/expiration headers + envelope shape), 410 maps to `unregistered`, oversize rejected with a boundary test at exactly 4096 bytes, JWT cached across pushes and refreshed after expiry.

# notify-relay Crate

Last verified: 2026-07-26

## Purpose

The notification relay: a **blind courier** between a self-hosted Custos instance and APNs.
APNs auth keys are bundle-ID-bound, so a self-hoster cannot push to the official iOS apps
directly — a relay is structurally required. It is trusted for *availability only*: payloads
reach it already HPKE-sealed to a per-device key, so neither the relay nor Apple ever sees
plaintext, and the relay holds no key material belonging to an instance or a device.

Architecture: [`docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md`](../../docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md).
Implementation detail: [`docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md`](../../docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md).

Its own binary and its own SQLite database — nothing is shared with the pds crate at
runtime. The conventions *are* shared: pattern comments, `db/` submodules owning queries
while cross-table sequences live above them, and `VNNN__*.sql` migrations behind a manifest
plus runner (copied, not shared — the runner is ~50 lines and the two crates' migration
histories are independent).

## Module Map

```text
src/
  main.rs        — CLI (serve, `mint-code --ttl`), config load, store open, endpoint bind, accept loop, shutdown
  config.rs      — TOML + `EZPDS_NOTIFY_*` env overlay, validated once into an immutable `Config`
  identity.rs    — the persistent iroh node secret key file (64 hex chars, created 0600, refused if wider)
  protocol.rs    — the `ezpds/notify/0` wire types: `Request`/`Response`/`PushOutcome`, the ALPN, the 64 KiB cap
  transport.rs   — iroh endpoint bind + accept loop; one JSON RPC per bidi stream, FIN-delimited, 30 s deadline
  service.rs     — RPC dispatch: the authorization order and the cross-table enrollment transaction
  rate_limit.rs  — in-memory per-node token buckets (registration + push budgets)
...

2	# notify-relay Crate
3	
4	Last verified: 2026-07-26
5	
6	## Purpose
7	
8	The notification relay: a **blind courier** between a self-hosted Custos instance and APNs.
9	APNs auth keys are bundle-ID-bound, so a self-hoster cannot push to the official iOS apps
10	directly — a relay is structurally required. It is trusted for *availability only*: payloads
11	reach it already HPKE-sealed to a per-device key, so neither the relay nor Apple ever sees
12	plaintext, and the relay holds no key material belonging to an instance or a device.
13	
14	Architecture: [`docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md`](../../docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md).
15	Implementation detail: [`docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md`](../../docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md).
16	
17	Its own binary and its own SQLite database — nothing is shared with the pds crate at
18	runtime. The conventions *are* shared: pattern comments, `db/` submodules owning queries
19	while cross-table sequences live above them, and `VNNN__*.sql` migrations behind a manifest
20	plus runner (copied, not shared — the runner is ~50 lines and the two crates' migration
21	histories are independent).
22	
23	## Module Map
24	
25	```text
26	src/
27	  main.rs        — CLI (serve, `mint-code --ttl`), config load, store open, endpoint bind, accept loop, shutdown
28	  config.rs      — TOML + `EZPDS_NOTIFY_*` env overlay, validated once into an immutable `Config`
29	  identity.rs    — the persistent iroh node secret key file (64 hex chars, created 0600, refused if wider)
30	  protocol.rs    — the `ezpds/notify/0` wire types: `Request`/`Response`/`PushOutcome`, the ALPN, the 64 KiB cap
31	  transport.rs   — iroh endpoint bind + accept loop; one JSON RPC per bidi stream, FIN-delimited, 30 s deadline
32	  service.rs     — RPC dispatch: the authorization order and the cross-table enrollment transaction
33	  rate_limit.rs  — in-memory per-node token buckets (registration + push budgets)
34	  db/            — `enrollment_codes`, `enrollments`, `handles`, plus the pool/migration runner
35	```
36	
37	## Security Invariants
38	
39	**The caller's identity is the connection, never the message.** `service.rs` is only ever
40	called with `connection.remote_id()`. No request field names a node, so there is nothing to
41	forge — iroh has verified the peer's key before the first application byte arrives. Do not
42	add a "node id" field to any request.
43	
44	**Every RPC except `enroll` requires enrollment, checked before the rate-limit charge.** An
45	unenrolled node is rejected on a cheap read, so it can neither spend an enrolled node's
46	budget nor build one against an identity it has not earned.
47	
48	**Handle queries are always scoped by node id.** `db/handles.rs` binds the caller's node id
49	into every WHERE clause; that is the whole cross-tenant boundary. A handle owned by another
50	node reads exactly like one that never existed (`unknownHandle` on push, a silent no-op on
51	drop) — the response must never become an ownership oracle.
52	
53	**Refusals are shape-uniform.** An enrollment code that is unknown, spent, or expired — and
54	an enroll with no code at all — all answer `denied`, so probing teaches nothing about which
55	codes the operator has minted. Storage failures answer with a fixed reason and are logged,
56	never reflected; an unparseable request is never echoed back.
57	
58	## Configuration
59	
60	TOML file (default `./notify-relay.toml`, or `--config`/`EZPDS_NOTIFY_CONFIG`) overlaid by
61	`EZPDS_NOTIFY_*` environment variables, which always win — the container deployment sets
62	everything that way and ships no file.
63	
64	| Setting | Env | Default |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `database_url` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_DATABASE_URL` | `notify-relay.db` |
67	| `secret_key_path` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_SECRET_KEY_PATH` | `notify-relay-node.key` |
68	| `ipv6` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_IPV6` | `true` (set false on a v4-only host) |
69	| `open_enrollment` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_OPEN_ENROLLMENT` | `false` |
70	| `apns.key_path` / `key_id` / `team_id` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_KEY_PATH` / `_KEY_ID` / `_TEAM_ID` | unset (all-or-nothing) |
71	| `apns.topics` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_TOPICS` (comma-separated) | empty = any topic |
72	| `apns.sandbox` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_SANDBOX` | `false` |
73	| `apns.endpoint` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL` | unset (the wiremock seam) |
74	| `rate_limits.*` | `EZPDS_NOTIFY_RATE_{REGISTRATIONS,PUSHES}_{PER_HOUR,BURST}` | 100/10 registrations, 1000/50 pushes per hour |
75	
76	The `[apns]` block is parsed and validated but unused until the push pipeline lands, so an
77	operator's deployment config does not change shape when pushes start working.
78	
79	## Operating
80	
81	```sh
82	notify-relay                      # serve; prints the node id instances dial
83	notify-relay mint-code --ttl 24h  # mint one single-use enrollment grant
84	```
85	
86	Enrollment codes are minted at the relay's own shell — there is deliberately no remote
87	admin surface. Relay state is re-derivable by re-enrollment, so backups are optional; the
88	node secret key file is not, since losing it re-addresses the relay.
89	
90	## Adding an RPC
91	
92	1. Add the variant to `Request`/`Response` in `protocol.rs` (camelCase tags) with a test
93	   pinning its wire shape.
94	2. Add the handler arm in `service.rs`, going through `require_enrolled` unless the RPC is
95	   deliberately pre-enrollment.
96	3. If it needs a new query, add it to the owning `db/` submodule — scoped by node id.
97	4. Cover it in `transport.rs`'s loopback tests, including the cross-tenant probe.

132	//! The `ezpds/notify/0` wire protocol: one JSON request per bidirectional iroh stream,
133	//! one JSON response back, the stream's FIN delimiting each.
134	//!
135	//! There is deliberately no credential anywhere in these messages. The caller's identity
136	//! is the QUIC connection's `remote_id()` — an instance proves who it is by holding its
137	//! node secret key, which iroh has already verified before the first byte arrives.
138	
139	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
140	
141	/// ALPN protocol identifier for the Custos↔relay notification channel. Bumped if the
142	/// wire protocol changes incompatibly. Distinct from the pds's `ezpds/iroh/0` tunnel.
143	pub const ALPN: &[u8] = b"ezpds/notify/0";
144	
145	/// Upper bound on one request (bytes) — bounds server-side allocation against a peer that
146	/// streams forever.
147	pub const MAX_MESSAGE_LEN: usize = 64 * 1024;
148	
149	/// A request from an instance.
150	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
151	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "camelCase")]
152	pub enum Request {
153	    /// Ask to be enrolled. Idempotent. `claimCode` is required unless the relay runs
154	    /// open enrollment.
155	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
156	    Enroll { claim_code: Option<String> },
157	    /// Register a device's APNs token, receiving an opaque handle for it.
158	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
159	    RegisterHandle {
160	        apns_token: String,
161	        apns_topic: String,
162	    },
163	    /// Forget a handle. Idempotent.
164	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
165	    DropHandle { handle: String },
166	    /// Deliver a sealed payload to the device behind `handle`.
167	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
168	    Push {
169	        handle: String,
170	        /// Which of the instance's versioned sender keys sealed this payload. Opaque to
171	        /// the relay — it is echoed to the device, never interpreted.
172	        kid: u32,
173	        /// Base64url HPKE encapsulated key.
174	        enc: String,
175	        /// Base64url HPKE ciphertext.
176	        ct: String,
177	        #[serde(default)]
178	        priority: Option<u8>,
179	        #[serde(default)]
180	        ttl_secs: Option<u32>,
181	        #[serde(default)]
182	        ping: Option<bool>,
183	    },
184	}
185	
186	/// What happened to a push. Reported inside a `pushed` response rather than as a
187	/// transport error, because every one of these is a normal outcome the sender acts on.
188	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
189	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
190	pub enum PushOutcome {
191	    /// Apple accepted the notification.
192	    Delivered,
193	    /// APNs 410: the device token is dead. The instance deletes its registration.
194	    Unregistered,
195	    /// This node's push budget is exhausted.
196	    Throttled,
197	    /// The serialized APNs request would exceed Apple's cap.
198	    TooLarge,
199	    /// The node has not enrolled with this relay.
200	    NotEnrolled,
201	    /// No such handle — or it belongs to another node, which reads identically.
202	    UnknownHandle,
203	    /// Apple refused, or the relay could not reach it.
204	    ApnsError,
205	}
206	
207	/// A response to an instance.
208	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
209	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "camelCase")]
210	pub enum Response {
211	    /// The request succeeded and carries nothing else to say.
212	    Ok,
213	    /// A handle was minted (or rotated).
214	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
215	    Handle { handle: String },
216	    /// A push finished, with its outcome.
217	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
218	    Pushed { outcome: PushOutcome },
219	    /// Enrollment was refused: no code, or a code that was unknown, spent, or expired.
220	    /// One shape for all of them — an enrollment probe learns nothing about which codes
221	    /// this relay has minted.
222	    Denied,
223	    /// The node must enroll before making this request.
224	    NotEnrolled,
225	    /// This node's request budget is exhausted; retry later.
226	    Throttled,
227	    /// The request could not be understood. Carries a short, non-reflective reason.
228	    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
229	    BadRequest { reason: String },
230	}
231	
232	#[cfg(test)]
233	mod tests {
234	    use super::*;
235	
236	    #[test]
237	    fn alpn_is_versioned_and_distinct_from_the_pds_tunnel() {
238	        assert_eq!(ALPN, b"ezpds/notify/0");
239	    }
240	
241	    #[test]
242	    fn requests_are_camel_case_tagged() {
243	        let json = r#"{"type":"registerHandle","apnsToken":"tok","apnsTopic":"org.obsign.app"}"#;
244	        assert_eq!(
245	            serde_json::from_str::<Request>(json).expect("parse"),
246	            Request::RegisterHandle {
247	                apns_token: "tok".into(),
248	                apns_topic: "org.obsign.app".into(),
249	            }
250	        );
251	    }
252	
253	    #[test]
254	    fn an_enroll_without_a_code_parses_as_none() {
255	        assert_eq!(
256	            serde_json::from_str::<Request>(r#"{"type":"enroll"}"#).expect("parse"),
257	            Request::Enroll { claim_code: None }
258	        );
259	    }
260	
261	    #[test]
262	    fn push_outcomes_render_as_camel_case() {
263	        let json = serde_json::to_string(&Response::Pushed {
264	            outcome: PushOutcome::UnknownHandle,
265	        })
266	        .expect("serialize");
267	        assert_eq!(json, r#"{"type":"pushed","outcome":"unknownHandle"}"#);
268	    }
269	}

271	// pattern: Mixed (Functional Core + I/O shell)
272	//
273	// Relay configuration: a TOML file overlaid with `EZPDS_NOTIFY_*` environment variables,
274	// mirroring the pds crate's `config_loader.rs` posture — parse into a `Raw*` shape whose
275	// fields are all optional, apply env overrides onto that shape, then validate once into
276	// the immutable `Config` the process runs on. The env map is passed in explicitly so tests
277	// never depend on the ambient environment.
278	//
279	// The APNs block is parsed and validated here but unused until the APNs pipeline lands;
280	// carrying it from the start means an operator's deployment config doesn't change shape
281	// when pushes start working.
282	
283	use std::collections::HashMap;
284	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
285	
286	use serde::Deserialize;
287	
288	/// Everything the relay needs to run.
289	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
290	pub struct Config {
291	    /// sqlx URL or plain filesystem path for the relay's own SQLite database.
292	    pub database_url: String,
293	    /// File holding the iroh node secret key (64 hex chars). Created on first run with
294	    /// 0600 permissions; the relay's node id — the address every instance dials — is
295	    /// derived from it, so losing the file re-addresses the relay.
296	    pub secret_key_path: PathBuf,
297	    /// Bind the IPv6 QUIC socket. False on a v4-only host (the `[iroh] ipv6` posture in
298	    /// the pds crate: without it, v6 relay probes fail `NetworkUnreachable` forever).
299	    pub ipv6: bool,
300	    /// Enroll any node that asks, with no enrollment code. Off by default: the official
301	    /// relay hands out codes, a self-run relay can skip the ceremony entirely.
302	    pub open_enrollment: bool,
303	    pub apns: ApnsConfig,
304	    pub rate_limits: RateLimitConfig,
305	}
306	
307	/// APNs credentials and the topic allowlist. Parsed now, used by the push pipeline.
308	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
309	pub struct ApnsConfig {
310	    /// Path to the `.p8` token-auth key.
311	    pub key_path: Option<PathBuf>,
312	    /// The `.p8` key's identifier (the JWT header `kid`).
313	    pub key_id: Option<String>,
314	    /// Apple developer team id (the JWT `iss`).
315	    pub team_id: Option<String>,
316	    /// Bundle ids this relay is willing to push to. Empty means "any topic" — the
317	    /// self-run posture, where the operator owns every app that could register.
318	    pub topics: Vec<String>,
319	    /// Use Apple's sandbox host rather than production.
320	    pub sandbox: bool,
321	    /// Endpoint override, the wiremock seam (`EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL`), mirroring
322	    /// `EZPDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL` in the pds crate.
323	    pub endpoint: Option<String>,
324	}
325	
326	/// Token-bucket sizes, per node id. Zero disables that bucket entirely.
327	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
328	pub struct RateLimitConfig {
329	    /// Sustained registration RPCs (`enroll`/`registerHandle`/`dropHandle`) per hour.
330	    pub registrations_per_hour: u32,
331	    /// Burst capacity for registration RPCs.
332	    pub registrations_burst: u32,
333	    /// Sustained pushes per hour.
334	    pub pushes_per_hour: u32,
335	    /// Burst capacity for pushes.
336	    pub pushes_burst: u32,
337	}
338	
339	impl Default for RateLimitConfig {
340	    fn default() -> Self {
341	        Self {
342	            registrations_per_hour: 100,
343	            registrations_burst: 10,
344	            pushes_per_hour: 1_000,
345	            pushes_burst: 50,
346	        }
347	    }
348	}
349	
350	/// Configuration failures, kept separate from I/O so a missing file reads differently
351	/// from a malformed one.
352	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
353	pub enum ConfigError {
354	    #[error("failed to read config file {path}: {source}")]
355	    Io {
356	        path: PathBuf,
357	        source: std::io::Error,
358	    },
359	    #[error("failed to parse config file: {0}")]
360	    Parse(#[from] toml::de::Error),
361	    #[error("invalid configuration: {0}")]
362	    Invalid(String),
363	}
364	
365	// ── Raw (all-optional) shapes ─────────────────────────────────────────────
366	
367	#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
368	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
369	pub struct RawConfig {
370	    database_url: Option<String>,
371	    secret_key_path: Option<String>,
372	    ipv6: Option<bool>,
373	    open_enrollment: Option<bool>,
374	    #[serde(default)]
375	    apns: RawApns,
376	    #[serde(default)]
377	    rate_limits: RawRateLimits,
378	}
379	
380	#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
381	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
382	struct RawApns {
383	    key_path: Option<String>,
384	    key_id: Option<String>,
385	    team_id: Option<String>,
386	    topics: Option<Vec<String>>,
387	    sandbox: Option<bool>,
388	    endpoint: Option<String>,
389	}
390	
391	#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
392	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
393	struct RawRateLimits {
394	    registrations_per_hour: Option<u32>,
395	    registrations_burst: Option<u32>,
396	    pushes_per_hour: Option<u32>,
397	    pushes_burst: Option<u32>,
398	}
399	
400	// ── Env overlay + validation (Functional Core) ────────────────────────────
401	
402	fn parse_bool(key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<bool, ConfigError> {
403	    match value {
404	        "true" | "1" => Ok(true),
405	        "false" | "0" => Ok(false),
406	        other => Err(ConfigError::Invalid(format!(
407	            "{key} must be true or false, got {other:?}"
408	        ))),
409	    }
410	}
411	
412	fn parse_u32(key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<u32, ConfigError> {
413	    value
414	        .parse()
415	        .map_err(|_| ConfigError::Invalid(format!("{key} must be a non-negative integer")))
416	}
417	
418	/// Overlay `EZPDS_NOTIFY_*` variables onto a parsed TOML shape. Env always wins — the
419	/// container deployment sets everything this way and never ships a file.
420	pub fn apply_env_overrides(
421	    mut raw: RawConfig,
422	    env: &HashMap<String, String>,
423	) -> Result<RawConfig, ConfigError> {
424	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_DATABASE_URL") {
425	        raw.database_url = Some(v.clone());
426	    }
427	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_SECRET_KEY_PATH") {
428	        raw.secret_key_path = Some(v.clone());
429	    }
430	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_IPV6") {
431	        raw.ipv6 = Some(parse_bool("EZPDS_NOTIFY_IPV6", v)?);
432	    }
433	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_OPEN_ENROLLMENT") {
434	        raw.open_enrollment = Some(parse_bool("EZPDS_NOTIFY_OPEN_ENROLLMENT", v)?);
435	    }
436	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_KEY_PATH") {
437	        raw.apns.key_path = Some(v.clone());
438	    }
439	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_KEY_ID") {
440	        raw.apns.key_id = Some(v.clone());
441	    }
442	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_TEAM_ID") {
443	        raw.apns.team_id = Some(v.clone());
444	    }
445	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_TOPICS") {
446	        raw.apns.topics = Some(
447	            v.split(',')
448	                .map(str::trim)
449	                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
450	                .map(str::to_owned)
451	                .collect(),
452	        );
453	    }
454	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_SANDBOX") {
455	        raw.apns.sandbox = Some(parse_bool("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_SANDBOX", v)?);
456	    }
457	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL") {
458	        raw.apns.endpoint = Some(v.clone());
459	    }
460	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_RATE_REGISTRATIONS_PER_HOUR") {
461	        raw.rate_limits.registrations_per_hour =
462	            Some(parse_u32("EZPDS_NOTIFY_RATE_REGISTRATIONS_PER_HOUR", v)?);
463	    }
464	    if let Some(v) = env.get("EZPDS_NOTIFY_RATE_REGISTRATIONS_BURST") {
465	        raw.rate_limits.registrations_burst =
466	            Some(parse_u32("EZPDS_NOTIFY_RATE_REGISTRATIONS_BURST", v)?);
467	    }

684	// pattern: Mixed (Functional Core + process-level state)
685	//
686	// Per-node token buckets. In-memory only: a restart forgives everyone, which is the right
687	// trade for a relay whose entire state is re-derivable by re-enrollment — persisting a
688	// limiter would buy an attacker nothing and cost every restart a write amplification.
689	//
690	// The bucket arithmetic is pure (`TokenBucket::take_at`), so exhaustion and refill are
691	// tested against an explicit clock rather than by sleeping.
692	
693	use std::collections::HashMap;
694	use std::sync::Mutex;
695	use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
696	
697	use crate::config::RateLimitConfig;
698	
699	/// A classic token bucket: `capacity` tokens, refilled at `per_second`.
700	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
701	struct TokenBucket {
702	    tokens: f64,
703	    last_refill: Instant,
704	}
705	
706	impl TokenBucket {
707	    fn new(capacity: u32, now: Instant) -> Self {
708	        Self {
709	            tokens: f64::from(capacity),
710	            last_refill: now,
711	        }
712	    }
713	
714	    /// Refill for the elapsed time, then take one token if there is one.
715	    fn take_at(&mut self, capacity: u32, per_second: f64, now: Instant) -> bool {
716	        let elapsed = now
717	            .saturating_duration_since(self.last_refill)
718	            .as_secs_f64();
719	        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed * per_second).min(f64::from(capacity));
720	        self.last_refill = now;
721	        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {
722	            self.tokens -= 1.0;
723	            true
724	        } else {
725	            false
726	        }
727	    }
728	}
729	
730	/// Which budget a request spends from. Registration RPCs and pushes are separate so a
731	/// chatty push load can never lock a node out of dropping a dead handle.
732	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
733	pub enum Bucket {
734	    Registration,
735	    Push,
736	}
737	
738	/// The process-level limiter: one bucket per (node id, bucket kind).
739	#[derive(Debug)]
740	pub struct RateLimiter {
741	    config: RateLimitConfig,
742	    buckets: Mutex<HashMap<(String, Bucket), TokenBucket>>,
743	}
744	
745	/// How long an untouched bucket is kept before the next sweep drops it. Well past a full
746	/// refill at any sane rate, so pruning can never hand back budget.
747	const IDLE_EVICTION: Duration = Duration::from_secs(6 * 3600);
748	
749	/// Prune when the map grows past this, so a flood of one-shot node ids cannot grow it
750	/// without bound between real requests.
751	const PRUNE_THRESHOLD: usize = 1024;
752	
753	impl RateLimiter {
754	    pub fn new(config: RateLimitConfig) -> Self {
755	        Self {
756	            config,
757	            buckets: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
758	        }
759	    }
760	
761	    /// The (capacity, refill-per-second) pair for a bucket kind. A per-hour rate of zero
762	    /// disables the limiter entirely.
763	    fn limits(&self, bucket: Bucket) -> Option<(u32, f64)> {
764	        let (per_hour, burst) = match bucket {
765	            Bucket::Registration => (
766	                self.config.registrations_per_hour,
767	                self.config.registrations_burst,
768	            ),
769	            Bucket::Push => (self.config.pushes_per_hour, self.config.pushes_burst),
770	        };
771	        if per_hour == 0 {
772	            return None;
773	        }
774	        Some((burst, f64::from(per_hour) / 3600.0))
775	    }
776	
777	    /// Charge one request to `node_id`, returning false when the budget is exhausted.
778	    pub fn check(&self, node_id: &str, bucket: Bucket) -> bool {
779	        self.check_at(node_id, bucket, Instant::now())
780	    }
781	
782	    /// `check` against an explicit clock, so the exhaustion/refill behaviour is testable
783	    /// without sleeping.
784	    pub fn check_at(&self, node_id: &str, bucket: Bucket, now: Instant) -> bool {
785	        let Some((capacity, per_second)) = self.limits(bucket) else {
786	            return true;
787	        };
788	        let mut buckets = self
789	            .buckets
790	            .lock()
791	            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
792	        if buckets.len() > PRUNE_THRESHOLD {
793	            buckets.retain(|_, b| now.saturating_duration_since(b.last_refill) < IDLE_EVICTION);
794	        }
795	        let entry = buckets
796	            .entry((node_id.to_owned(), bucket))
797	            .or_insert_with(|| TokenBucket::new(capacity, now));
798	        entry.take_at(capacity, per_second, now)
799	    }
800	}

3	// The handle store. A handle is 128 bits of randomness standing in for one device's APNs
4	// token; the instance sends the handle, never the token, so a compromised relay database
5	// still cannot be correlated with anything an instance said before enrolling.
6	//
7	// Every query here takes the caller's node id and binds it into the WHERE clause. That is
8	// the whole cross-tenant boundary: a handle belonging to node B is, for node A, exactly as
9	// resolvable as one that never existed.

11	use sqlx::SqlitePool;
12	
13	/// A handle row as its owner may see it.
14	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
15	pub struct HandleRow {
16	    pub handle: String,
17	    pub apns_token: String,
18	    pub apns_topic: String,
19	}
20	
21	/// Register (or re-register) a device for `node_id`, returning the live handle.
22	///
23	/// Re-registering the same `(node_id, apns_token)` **rotates** the handle: the old one
24	/// stops resolving in the same transaction the new one starts. Rotation is the point —
25	/// a handle that outlived its registration would be a stale capability.
26	pub async fn register_handle(
27	    db: &SqlitePool,
28	    node_id: &str,
29	    apns_token: &str,
30	    apns_topic: &str,
31	    handle: &str,
32	) -> Result<String, sqlx::Error> {
33	    let mut tx = db.begin().await?;
34	    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM handles WHERE node_id = ? AND apns_token = ?")
35	        .bind(node_id)
36	        .bind(apns_token)
37	        .execute(&mut *tx)
38	        .await?;
39	    sqlx::query(
40	        "INSERT INTO handles (handle, node_id, apns_token, apns_topic, created_at) \
41	         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'))",
42	    )
43	    .bind(handle)
44	    .bind(node_id)
45	    .bind(apns_token)
46	    .bind(apns_topic)
47	    .execute(&mut *tx)
48	    .await?;
49	    tx.commit().await?;
50	    Ok(handle.to_owned())
51	}

53	/// Resolve a handle **owned by** `node_id`. `None` covers both "no such handle" and
54	/// "someone else's handle" — the caller must not distinguish them.
55	pub async fn resolve_handle(
56	    db: &SqlitePool,
57	    node_id: &str,
58	    handle: &str,
59	) -> Result<Option<HandleRow>, sqlx::Error> {
60	    let row = sqlx::query_as::<_, (String, String, String)>(
61	        "SELECT handle, apns_token, apns_topic FROM handles WHERE handle = ? AND node_id = ?",
62	    )
63	    .bind(handle)
64	    .bind(node_id)
65	    .fetch_optional(db)
66	    .await?;
67	
68	    Ok(row.map(|(handle, apns_token, apns_topic)| HandleRow {
69	        handle,
70	        apns_token,
71	        apns_topic,
72	    }))
73	}

75	/// Drop a handle owned by `node_id`. Idempotent; reports whether a row was removed so the
76	/// relay can log real deletions without telling the caller anything either way.
77	pub async fn drop_handle(
78	    db: &SqlitePool,
79	    node_id: &str,
80	    handle: &str,
81	) -> Result<bool, sqlx::Error> {
82	    let result = sqlx::query("DELETE FROM handles WHERE handle = ? AND node_id = ?")
83	        .bind(handle)
84	        .bind(node_id)
85	        .execute(db)
86	        .await?;
87	    Ok(result.rows_affected() == 1)

--- dev-deps section ---
# objc2 core (Retained, AnyThread) + the BackgroundTasks framework binding for the
# wallet's iOS background media-backup scheduling (bg_backup.rs), and block2 for the
# BGTaskScheduler launch/expiration handler blocks. Same objc2 0.6 family as
# objc2-foundation, so the lockfile stays on one major. iOS-only at the use site.
objc2 = "0.6"
objc2-background-tasks = "0.3"
block2 = "0.6"
# SCNetworkReachability WWAN flag for the wallet's "Wi-Fi only" background-backup setting
# (bg_backup.rs) — BGProcessingTaskRequest can't express metered-network avoidance, so the
# sweep checks the live network type at fire time. Already in the tree transitively
# (hickory-resolver/reqwest); promoted to a direct iOS-target dep at the use site.
system-configuration = "0.7"
rand_core = { version = "0.6", features = ["getrandom"] }
base64 = "0.21"
ciborium = "0.2"
data-encoding = "2"
sha2 = "0.10"
# HMAC-SHA256 for the blob mirror's AWS SigV4 request signing (pds) — same RustCrypto family
# as sha2/hkdf, already resolved transitively.
hmac = "0.12"
# HKDF-SHA256 for deriving the recovery keypair from the escrow seed (same RustCrypto family as
# sha2/hmac, already resolved transitively via reqwest/rustls).
hkdf = "0.12"
# RFC 9180 HPKE for the notification relay's sealed payloads (crypto). 0.13, not 0.14:
# 0.14 pulls its own p256 0.14 / aes-gcm 0.11 / hkdf 0.13 line (plus p384 + p521, which its
# coarse `nistp` feature can't exclude), compiling a second major of three crypto crates the
# workspace deliberately keeps single-major. 0.13 resolves onto the existing p256 0.13 /
# aes-gcm 0.10 / hkdf 0.12 and its per-curve `p256` feature drags in nothing else. Same RFC,
# same pinned suite. default-features = false drops x25519.
hpke = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["alloc", "p256"] }
# hpke 0.13 takes its CSPRNG from rand_core 0.9 — already in the workspace tree alongside 0.6 and
# 0.10, so this adds no new major. It depends on rand_core with default features off, so
# `OsRng` isn't compiled in; this renamed alias turns the `os_rng` feature on for that same 0.9
# crate rather than adding a second copy. Renamed because `rand_core` above is the 0.6 line.
rand_core_os = { package = "rand_core", version = "0.9", features = ["os_rng"] }
zeroize = "1"
urlencoding = "2"
# QR-code matrix generation for the wallet-confirmed OAuth consent page (pds): the consent page
# renders a QR encoding the pending request's `request_id` so the identity wallet can scan it
# cross-device instead of typing the code. `qrcodegen` is the Nayuki reference encoder — pure Rust,
# MIT-licensed, zero transitive dependencies; the PDS renders the matrix to an inline SVG itself.

content.content:
# Notification Relay — Implementation Plan (MM-311)

[MM-311](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-311) · implementation leg of
[docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](2026-07-10-notification-relay.md)
(design PR #207, merged — that doc remains the architecture source of truth; this doc pins
the implementation details against the codebase and decomposes the work into issues).

**Codebase verified: 2026-07-17** (migrations at V051, bruno seq at 123, iroh 1.0.0,
workspace 0.5.2).

## Refinements to the design doc

Three details discovered during codebase verification refine (not reverse) the design:

1. **Registrations key on the account DID, not `devices.id`.** The design says the
   registration lands in "new columns/table beside `devices`" — but `devices` is a
   *transient pre-DID artifact*: rows are deleted inside the DID-promotion transaction
   (`routes/create_did.rs`) and the table FKs to `pending_accounts`. A registration FK'd
   there would die exactly when the account starts mattering. Wallet notification
   registrations therefore key on `(did, device_uuid)` where `device_uuid` is an
   app-generated stable identifier, are created **post-promotion** over the OAuth/DPoP
   channel (through the `authenticate_access` seam — the auth-seam-check applies), and are
   purged in `account_delete::purge_account`'s explicit FK-ordered delete list.
   Admin-companion registrations are a separate table keyed by `admin_devices.id`,
   cleaned up alongside the revoke tombstone. Pending (pre-DID) accounts get no pushes —
   onboarding completes with promotion, and registration is one of the first
   post-promotion calls.
2. **The ciphersuite is forced to AES-256-GCM.** CryptoKit ships exactly one P-256 HPKE
   suite: `HPKE.Ciphersuite.P256_SHA256_AES_GCM_256`. So the wire suite is pinned to
   **DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM, mode_auth** — no
   negotiation, ever; `v` in the envelope names the whole suite. RFC 9180's appendix has
   no test vector for this exact combo (A.3 is AES-128), so golden fixtures are generated
   from the Rust implementation, pinned in `crates/crypto/tests/fixtures/`, and
   cross-verified against CryptoKit by an on-device XCTest in the wallet phase.
3. **The v1 back-channel is the RPC response, not a server-initiated stream.** The relay
   calls APNs synchronously inside the push RPC, so `410 Unregistered` (and throttle/size
   outcomes) return in the same request/response exchange over the already-open bidi
   stream. No relay-initiated streams in v1 — that machinery (delivery receipts) stays
   out of scope, as the design already decided.

CryptoKit's HPKE API requires **iOS 17**; the apps' deployment target currently rides
tauri-cli's default (13.0, nothing overridden in either `tauri.conf.json`). Decision:
raise `bundle > iOS > minimumSystemVersion` to `17.0` for both apps in the wallet phase.
Both apps are new (no installed base below 17), and a per-target split (NSE at 17, app
lower, runtime-gated registration) buys nothing but complexity.

## Wire formats

### Sealed payload (Custos → device, opaque to relay/Apple)

Plaintext (serde_json, camelCase):

```json
{ "type": "agent_claim_pending", "title": "…", "body": "…", "data": { … }, "pad": "…" }
```

`pad` is a string of `0x20` bytes sized so the **serialized APNs request** lands exactly
on a padding bucket (below). Sealed with HPKE mode_auth:

- suite: DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM
- `info = b"ezpds/notify/1"`, `aad = b""` (version binding lives in `info` + envelope `v`)
- sender key: the instance's static notification sender keypair named by `kid`
- recipient key: the device's notification public key

### APNs payload (relay → Apple → device)

```json
{
  "aps": { "alert": { "title": "Custos", "body": "Encrypted notification" },
           "mutable-content": 1 },
  "ezpds": { "v": 1, "kid": 3, "enc": "<b64url encapsulated key>", "ct": "<b64url ciphertext>" }
}
```

Ping mode (later phase) replaces `aps` with `{ "content-available": 1 }` and omits
`ezpds` entirely.

### Padding buckets

Buckets are defined on the **serialized APNs JSON body**: `{1024, 2048, 3584}` bytes
(3584 keeps headroom under APNs' 4096 cap). Base64url expansion is deterministic
(`enc` = 65-byte uncompressed P-256 point → 87 chars; `ct` = plaintext + 16-byte tag),
so Custos computes the exact `pad` length that makes the final body hit the smallest
bucket ≥ the unpadded size, and refuses payloads that exceed the largest bucket. A
relay-side check enforces the same cap defensively, with a boundary test at exactly
4096 bytes.

### Custos ↔ relay RPC (`ezpds/notify/0`)

New ALPN beside `ezpds/iroh/0`. One JSON request per bidi stream, response JSON, stream
FIN delimits (the `iroh_tunnel.rs` pattern: `read_to_end` with a 64 KiB cap, 30 s
per-stream timeout). The dialing node's identity is `connection.remote_id()` — no
credential in the messages. Requests are a tagged enum:

| request | response | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `enroll { claimCode? }` | `ok` / `denied` | idempotent; `claimCode` required unless the relay runs open enrollment |
| `registerHandle { apnsToken, apnsTopic }` | `{ handle }` | topic must be in the relay's served-topic set; re-registering the same token rotates the handle |
| `dropHandle { handle }` | `ok` | idempotent |
| `push { handle, kid, enc, ct, priority, ttlSecs, ping }` | `{ outcome }` | outcome ∈ `delivered · unregistered · throttled · tooLarge · notEnrolled · unknownHandle · apnsError` |

`unregistered` is the APNs 410 feedback: Custos deletes the registration row on receipt.
Every request except `enroll` requires the node id to be enrolled; handles are only ever
resolvable by the node id that registered them.

The Custos side gains its first **outbound** iroh leg: a `notify_relay_client` module that
reuses the existing `IrohState` endpoint (an iroh `Endpoint` both accepts and dials),
dials by node id from config, opens one stream per RPC, and reconnects lazily with
exponential backoff. Sends are fire-and-forget from callers' perspective: triggers enqueue
into an in-process `tokio::sync::mpsc` worker so a dead relay never blocks a request path.
v1 queue is in-memory only (a missed push is a missed banner, not lost data — the app
reconciles from its Custos); durable queuing is an explicit non-goal.

## The relay: `crates/notify-relay/`

New workspace member; own binary, own SQLite DB, same stack (tokio + iroh + sqlx +
tracing; axum only if/when an HTTP surface appears — v1 has none). Modeled on the pds
crate's conventions: pattern comments, `db/` submodules own queries, migrations as
`VNNN__*.sql` with the same manifest/runner pattern (copied small, not shared — the
runner is ~50 lines and the crates' migration histories are independent).

enrollment_codes(code TEXT PK, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                 consumed_at TEXT, consumed_by_node TEXT)          -- V001
enrollments(node_id TEXT PK, enrolled_at TEXT NOT NULL, code_used TEXT)
handles(handle TEXT PK,                    -- 128-bit random, base64url
        node_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES enrollments(node_id),
        apns_token TEXT NOT NULL, apns_topic TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL, last_push_at TEXT)
```

Status is derived from timestamps (the `claim_codes` doctrine); enrollment-code redemption
is the same atomic guarded-UPDATE shape as `consume_pairing_code`. `(node_id, apns_token)`
unique — re-registration rotates the handle in place.

**Config** (TOML + env, mirroring `config_loader.rs` posture): iroh secret key path
(file-persisted — the relay has no master-key hierarchy; 0600 perms), `open_enrollment: bool`
(default false), APNs: `.p8` path, key id, team id, served topics list, endpoint override
(`EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL` — the wiremock seam, same trick as `EZPDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL`),
sandbox/production toggle. Enrollment codes are minted by a CLI subcommand
(`notify-relay mint-code --ttl 60m`) — operator-local, no remote admin surface in v1.

**APNs client:** reqwest (workspace 0.13, rustls — ALPN-negotiates h2 against real APNs,
h1 against wiremock). Token auth is a hand-rolled ES256 JWT over the existing `p256`
dep (header `{alg, kid}` + claims `{iss: team_id, iat}`, base64url, ECDSA-sign — ~30
lines; avoids `jsonwebtoken`'s `ring` dependency), cached and refreshed at 50 minutes
per Apple's 20–60 min rule. Headers per push: `apns-topic` (from the handle row),
`apns-push-type: alert` (or `background` for ping), `apns-priority` (10 alert / 5 ping),
`apns-expiration` (now + ttlSecs).

**Rate limits:** in-memory token buckets (no persistence — restart forgiveness is fine),
two keys: per node id (default 1 000/h, burst 50) and per handle (default 60/h, burst 10);
exceeded → `throttled`. Registration RPCs get a per-node bucket too (default 100/h).

**Deploy:** a second binary means the root single-binary Dockerfile doesn't cover it; the
relay ships its own `crates/notify-relay/Dockerfile` (same builder pattern,
`cargo build --release --locked -p notify-relay`) deployed as a Railway service beside
pds/mcp-sidecar, Litestream optional (state is re-derivable by re-enrollment — the design
already accepts relay state loss). Ops docs in the final phase.

default `None` → feature off, the `[iroh]` posture), `enrollment_code: Option<String>`
(consumed on first successful enroll), `ping_mode: bool` (later phase). Env:
`EZPDS_NOTIFICATIONS_RELAY`, `EZPDS_NOTIFICATIONS_ENROLLMENT_CODE`. Requires
`[iroh] enabled` (validation error otherwise — the endpoint is the dialer).

-- The relay's whole world: who may talk to it, and which opaque handles they own.
--
-- No DIDs, no account handles, no raw device tokens beyond the APNs token Apple itself
-- requires — the relay is a blind courier, and this schema is the limit of what it knows.

-- Enrollment grants, minted by the operator (`notify-relay mint-code`). Status is derived
-- from the timestamps rather than stored (the pds crate's claim_codes doctrine): a code is
-- pending while unconsumed and unexpired, and redemption is a single guarded UPDATE.
CREATE TABLE enrollment_codes (
    code             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
    consumed_at      TEXT,
    consumed_by_node TEXT
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- Instances allowed to register handles and push. `code_used` is NULL for a node enrolled
-- under open enrollment, which is exactly the audit distinction an operator wants.
CREATE TABLE enrollments (
    node_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    enrolled_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    code_used   TEXT
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- Opaque push handles: 128 bits of randomness standing in for a device's APNs token, so
-- an instance never re-sends the token and the relay never correlates one across nodes.
CREATE TABLE handles (
    handle       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    node_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES enrollments(node_id),
    apns_token   TEXT NOT NULL,
    apns_topic   TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_push_at TEXT
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- One live handle per (node, token): re-registering the same device rotates the handle
-- rather than accumulating aliases for it.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX handles_node_token ON handles (node_id, apns_token);

-- Every lookup is scoped by the registering node id, so it leads the index.
CREATE INDEX handles_node ON handles (node_id);

==> changelog.d/README.md <==
# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text

==> changelog.d/mm-415.added.md <==
Groundwork for encrypted push notifications: Custos gained the sealing layer that will let a self-hosted instance send notifications through a relay it does not have to trust. Payloads are sealed to a per-device key with HPKE (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-256-GCM, authenticated mode), so a relay operator and Apple both see only opaque bytes and neither can forge a notification your device will accept. Payloads are also padded up to one of three fixed sizes: that does not hide length outright, but it reduces what length can reveal from a per-notification fingerprint to which of three buckets a notification fell into. Nothing is enabled by this change on its own; the relay, the registration flow, and the on-device decryption arrive in the phases that follow.

==> changelog.d/mm-416.added.md <==
New `notify-relay` service: a blind courier that self-hosted Custos instances enroll with over iroh (`ezpds/notify/0`) to obtain opaque push handles for their devices. Enrollment is closed by default and gated on operator-minted single-use codes (`notify-relay mint-code --ttl 60m`); `open_enrollment = true` admits any instance on a self-run relay. Handles are resolvable only by the instance that registered them, and per-instance rate limits apply. Sending pushes to Apple arrives in a following change.

==> changelog.d/mm-456.added.md <==
A recovery key for identities hosted anywhere. Until now, the wallet's Shamir recovery seed came bundled with Custos escrow, so an identity you imported from bsky.social or any other spec-compliant PDS got a Secure-Enclave root key, monitoring, and backups — but no way back in if you lost the device. The new "Add a recovery key" flow on the identity screen is the same ceremony minus the escrow: the wallet generates the seed, splits it 2-of-3, and publishes a device-key-signed operation that inserts the derived recovery key straight after your device key. Nothing is removed, and no share — nor any part of the recovery key — is ever sent to your PDS; the only thing the wallet asks it is the public question of whether it offers recovery escrow at all. Share 1 goes to your Keychain to sync across your Apple devices; Shares 2 and 3 are both yours to save, and any two of the three restore the identity through the existing recovery ceremony. The flow is offered only where it is the right answer: on a server that advertises recovery escrow, the escrow-backed upgrade is offered instead, and on a server that could not be reached nothing is offered at all rather than guessing. If you later move to a host that does hold shares, the wallet offers escrow once — as an option, not a reminder.

==> changelog.d/mm-457.added.md <==
App passwords, handle changes, identity removal, and media restore now work on any server. Four features that are pure standard AT Protocol have been dark for identities hosted anywhere but Custos, for a single reason: each needs a full sign-in, and the only sign-in the wallet knew how to perform was the passwordless one that a Custos server offers. On bsky.social or the reference PDS there was no such option, so the buttons were there and the session behind them was not. The wallet now asks the identity's server which sign-in it supports and offers the right one: a Face ID unlock where the server accepts a device-key signature, and a prompt for your account password where it does not — with emailed two-factor codes handled, and the password sent once, to your own server, and never stored. From then on the session behaves identically either way: it refreshes on its own, and it is discarded if your identity moves to a different host. A server the wallet could not reach is never assumed to lack passwordless sign-in — it keeps offering the unlock it already used, because a network hiccup is not a fact about your server.

==> changelog.d/mm-458.added.md <==
--- script ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Require a changelog fragment *added by the change itself* when a PR changes a shipped
# surface (fragments already sitting in changelog.d/ from other work don't satisfy it).
# CHANGELOG_BASE_REF is set to the PR base SHA in CI; an explicit first argument is
# convenient for local checks. With neither, fragment validity is still checked but
# presence is not required because there is no trustworthy comparison range.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

base_ref="${1:-${CHANGELOG_BASE_REF:-}}"
fragment_dir="changelog.d"
fragment_re='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.(added|changed|fixed|removed|security)\.md$'

fail=0
fragment_count=0
while IFS= read -r fragment; do
  name="${fragment##*/}"
  if ! [[ "$name" =~ $fragment_re ]]; then
    echo "✗ invalid changelog fragment '$fragment' — expected <id>.<added|changed|fixed|removed|security>.md" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  if ! grep -q '[^[:space:]]' "$fragment"; then
    echo "✗ changelog fragment '$fragment' is empty" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  fragment_count=$((fragment_count + 1))
done < <(find "$fragment_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' ! -name README.md | sort)

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$base_ref" ]; then
  echo "✓ $fragment_count valid changelog fragment(s); no base ref supplied, so presence was not evaluated"
  exit 0
fi

content.thinking:
I'm starting with the core APNS module and thinking through the structure carefully. I'm setting up the imports for cryptographic signing with ECDSA and time utilities to handle the relay logic.

Now I'm defining the constants and types that shape the protocol — the 4096-byte payload limit Apple enforces, the 50-minute token lifetime, and the production versus sandbox endpoints. I'm also sketching out the error types and the `PushRequest` struct that captures what the relay needs to send.

I'm hitting a design question about the `ping` field — since it's out of scope for this phase, I need to decide whether to ignore it or reject requests that have it set. The honest minimal approach feels right: reject rather than silently ignore.

Actually, I'm reconsidering. The ping mode is just a few extra lines — setting `content-available` to 1, omitting the `ezpds` key, using background push type, and priority 5. But the issue's scope is explicit: the alert envelope only. Phase 8 owns ping mode, so I'll keep it out of scope now and document that clearly in the code and in the agents guide to avoid silent failures.

Now I'm moving on to implement the JWT signing logic...

Writing JWT signing function... Implementing token caching with a lifetime check, then falling back to signing a fresh JWT if the cached one has expired. I'm also adding a testable variant that accepts a specific timestamp, and moving on to the `send` method that will handle the actual request dispatch.

For `send`, I need to add a size check that returns a `TooLarge` outcome if the payload exceeds limits. I'm building the request body by serializing the encrypted content, then setting up the headers with the JWT bearer token, APNS topic, push type, priority (which can come from the request or default to 10), and expiration time based on a TTL value.

If no TTL is provided, I'll default to one hour since older notifications lose their value anyway. The URL follows the APNS format with the device token, and I need to handle the case where credentials are missing — if the ApnsClient can't be initialized during service setup, the push should fail gracefully with an error log rather than panicking.

For the client initialization, I'm weighing options: I could pass `Option<ApnsClient>` into the constructor, but that breaks all the existing test call sites. A builder pattern with `with_apns()` keeps tests untouched and reads cleanly, though it risks silent misconfiguration if someone forgets to call it.

The safest approach is to have `main.rs` fail loudly at startup if APNs credentials are configured but the client can't be built — that way an operator won't end up with a relay that silently drops push notifications. I'll go with the builder pattern.

Now I'm setting up the per-handle rate limiting with config parameters for pushes per hour and burst capacity, plus corresponding environment variables.

For the push ordering, I need to check enrollment first, then node budget, resolve the handle (failing with UnknownHandle if needed), check per-handle budget (returning Throttled if exceeded), validate the message size (TooLarge if too big), and finally send. I'll charge the node budget before doing the work — it's consistent to charge first even for oversized messages that can't be delivered, since that's misbehavior on the sender's part.

When a push is delivered, I'll update the last_push_at timestamp, and I need to think through what happens on unregistered status with respect to pruning.

I'm going to prepare the file with a TODO for the user to implement `classify_status`, then ask them about it while I finish the rest.

Now I'm writing the APNS implementation. For the tests, I'll generate a test P-256 private key using `SigningKey::random` and convert it to PEM format with the pkcs8 feature — that gives me the encoding capability I need.

I'm setting the default TTL for APNS expiration to 3600 seconds, then moving on to configure the reqwest client. For version 0.13, I need to disable default features and explicitly enable JSON and rustls support — with only rustls specified, it becomes the default TLS backend without needing an explicit `.use_rustls_tls()` call.

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The **wiremock seam works because of ALPN**, not because of a code branch: `reqwest` + rustls negotiates `h2` against `https://api.push.apple.com` (Apple's provider API is HTTP/2-only) but falls back to HTTP/1.1 against a plain `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` mock. One client, no test-only transport path.
- **Hand-rolling ES256 costs ~30 lines because a P-256 ECDSA signature already *is* the JWS format.** `p256::ecdsa::Signature::to_bytes()` returns the fixed 64-byte `r‖s` concatenation that RFC 7515 specifies for ES256 — no DER unwrapping. Pulling `jsonwebtoken` would drag `ring` into a workspace that is otherwise pure-RustCrypto + rustls.
- The `.p8` Apple hands out is a **PKCS#8 PEM**, which is why I enabled p256's `pem` feature — it activates `pem-rfc7468`, already resolved at 0.7 in this tree, so `cargo deny`'s duplicate-major guard-bans stay satisfied.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Now the APNs module. I'm leaving one function for you to write — see below.

questions.question: When APNs answers 410 Unregistered, should the relay delete its own handle row, or keep it and only report `unregistered` back to the instance?

options.label: Report only, keep the row (Recommended)
options.description: The relay answers `unregistered` and leaves the handle intact. The instance deletes its registration and stops pushing; the row ages out when the device re-registers (which rotates it) or the instance calls dropHandle. Keeps the response idempotent — a lost RPC response means a retry still says `unregistered` rather than the ambiguous `unknownHandle`.

options.label: Delete the row too
options.description: The relay prunes eagerly, so a dead token can never be pushed to twice and the relay stops storing a token Apple has disowned. Cost: a retried push after a lost response answers `unknownHandle`, which reads to the instance as 'someone else's handle' rather than 'this device is gone'.

options.label: Delete, but keep a tombstone
options.description: Mark the row unregistered (a timestamp column) rather than deleting, so retries still answer `unregistered` and the token stops being usable. Costs a V002 migration and a nullable column this phase otherwise doesn't need.

questions.question: A push carries an optional `ttlSecs`. What should `apns-expiration` be when the sender omits it?

options.label: 1 hour (Recommended)
options.description: now + 3600. A notification banner an hour stale is worthless anyway, and Apple will hold it for a device that is briefly offline (commute, overnight airplane mode) instead of dropping it.

options.label: Immediate (expiration 0)
options.description: Apple attempts delivery once and discards on failure. Most privacy-preserving — nothing queues at Apple — but a phone that is off for two minutes silently misses the notification.

options.label: 24 hours
options.description: now + 86400. Maximises delivery, but a day-old 'agent claim pending' banner arriving after the claim already expired is actively misleading.
